readiness.reason: F-001 is confirmed in source (playlist.ts:83,87,91 with authFetch.ts:9-16): a failed playlist load leaves an empty playlist marked as saved, and a later save can overwrite the on-air day. Together with F-002, which logs all tabs out on a transient refresh failure, I would not recommend release until these are fixed. This is static review only, with no runtime or browser tests.

F-001.reason: I confirmed it in source. AuthFetchError has no status field, so e.status is always undefined, the error is swallowed, playlist is set to [] and markSaved() runs. A later save can overwrite the real day. I am treating it as a de facto blocker for on-air continuity.

F-002.reason: auth.ts:235-251 calls removeToken() on any non-ok or thrown refresh and broadcasts logout. A backend restart or update overlapping a refresh drops sessions in all tabs. HIGH, non-blocker.

F-003.reason: Accessibility is outside my scope. The peer evidence suggests the focus-management gap is real but is not a playout blocker.

F-007.reason: auth.ts:324 checks e.status, which is always undefined. A failed obtainUuid sets uuid to null, which makes streamUrl undefined (playoutStatus.ts:32), and the uuid watch at playoutStatus.ts:59-66 only reconnects once the uuid becomes truthy again. MEDIUM, non-blocker.

F-008.reason: config.ts:99-114 replaces the channel list with a hard-coded id 1 on any error, and only logs out on a 401. The channel id is then not server-provided.

F-009.reason: chunkedUpload.ts:76-120 has no sibling abort when one worker throws, and uploads.ts:178 allows a retry on the same batch id. This risks concurrent writers on one media file.

F-010.reason: playlist.ts:75-91 has no sequence guard and sets loadedKey after the await, so a stale response can win. I did not audit the dirty/save logic, so I would accept merging it into F-001.
